content.jointProblem: What mechanisms explain cracking at AutomVoj’s painted mild-steel conveyor-frame welds after prolonged chilled service, and could changes to welding procedure, filler material or joint geometry reduce crack initiation and growth? The first experiment would compare representative production joints under measured service loading at room temperature and 2–6 °C, with controlled moisture and thermal histories, to test whether the researcher’s thermo-mechanical fatigue methods transfer to these components.

rationale.text: Erić has directly investigated the interaction of mechanical fatigue and thermal cycling in welded structural steel, providing a relevant basis for testing AutomVoj’s suspected combined-loading mechanism.

sources.quote: Four loading programmes were applied: isothermal fatigue at 20 °C, isothermal fatigue at −30 °C, in-phase thermo-mechanical fatigue (TMF), and out-of-phase TMF

rationale.text: He has experience constructing fatigue assessments from operational strain and temperature measurements rather than relying solely on laboratory loading assumptions.

sources.quote: Rainflow-counted stress spectra and simultaneous temperature records were used to construct a combined loading environment for assessment.

rationale.text: His work combines weld residual-stress measurements with thermal–mechanical simulation, relevant to investigating whether welding-induced stresses contribute to the frame failures.

sources.quote: Residual stresses in as-welded and post-weld heat-treated (PWHT) T-joint specimens of S460M low-alloy steel were measured by hole-drilling with strain-gauge rosettes
compared with sequentially coupled thermal–mechanical FE simulations.

rationale.text: His group uses fatigue-testing and climate-control equipment that could address AutomVoj’s lack of low-temperature cyclic-testing capability, subject to configuration and access checks.

sources.quote: The group routinely uses servo-hydraulic fatigue testing machines, a climate chamber capable of reaching −60 °C

constraints.text: Testing must represent the painted mild-steel hollow-section connections and their actual chilled-service conditions; room-temperature load tests alone have not reproduced the failure.

sources.quote: Our conveyor frames are welded from mild steel hollow section and painted for corrosion resistance before delivery.
We test frames under load at room temperature and they pass without any problem.

constraints.text: Failure analysis must account for the limited retained failure material and use the existing site documentation; destructive sampling needs an agreed allocation.

sources.quote: We have photos and measurements of the cracked joints from site visits, and we still have two of the failed sections in storage.

constraints.text: The plan requires external low-temperature cyclic-testing capability and advance scheduling of the researcher's shared equipment.

sources.quote: We do not currently have the equipment or know-how to test at low temperatures under cyclic load.
Erić's climate chamber and servo-hydraulic machine are shared with two other research groups; scheduling access for extended test campaigns requires advance coordination.

constraints.text: Company engineering effort must be explicitly allocated around live projects because there is no dedicated R&D department.

sources.quote: We have no dedicated R&D department
our chief engineer and two senior automation engineers who allocate time between live projects and improvement work.

risks: The strongest thermo-mechanical evidence concerns plate joints and substantially sub-zero temperatures, not painted mild-steel hollow sections at 2–6 °C. Its mechanisms and quantitative models may not transfer; the first representative-joint experiment must test that transfer rather than assume cold-induced embrittlement.

Condensation-related corrosion, coating defects and manufacturing variability remain plausible contributors, but the supplied evidence does not establish the cause or demonstrate condensation-control capability in the available chamber.
An accelerated test may produce a different failure mechanism from the approximately 18-month service failure, particularly before operational load and thermal histories are measured.

Researcher availability, equipment booking dates, project budget, deadline and customer-site access are unknown. Shared laboratory equipment and limited company engineering capacity could delay the work.
questions: What are the exact steel grade, section dimensions, joint drawings, welding procedure, filler, weld inspection records and coating specification, and do these vary between failed and surviving frames?
Can the two failed sections be released for examination, and what destructive sampling is permitted after documenting crack origins and fracture surfaces?
Can customer sites provide access for strain, vibration, temperature and humidity monitoring, together with belt loads, operating cycles, washdown or defrost histories and installation details?
Can the laboratory reproduce the relevant mechanical loading, 2–6 °C conditions and condensation exposure for these specimens, and when are the chamber and fatigue machine available?
What time can Erić and AutomVoj’s engineers commit, and what budget and decision deadline are available for a joint project?
Which candidate manufacturing changes are feasible, and what comparison criteria, replication and follow-up service evidence would be required before adopting a change?
